_about: UNC Joint Fluids Lab wave tank (Chapman Hall) and its 30-piston wavemaker. Every length in metres. Each value carries how it was obtained and how sure it is; edit a value here and everything downstream (volumes, wave model, 3D model, drawings) follows. See MEASUREMENTS.md for the working behind each number.

frame.x: along the channel axis, 0 at the channel mouth (inside face of the head's channel-side wall), positive toward the reservoir
frame.y: across the axis, 0 on the centreline
frame.z: up, 0 on the inside of the tank floor

length.how: William 28 Oct: 16 windows down each side, with beams between them alternating 4, 5, 4, ... 4 in from the head-end corner to the reservoir (15 beams, 67 in). The channel's window width is ASSUMED equal to the head's measured 39.25 in (the photos' post spacing, 1.07 m with range 1.00-1.15, agrees with the 1.11 m this implies); corners read like the head's. 16 x 39.25 + 67 + 2 x 2 3/8 = 699.75 in. Replaces the 15.4 m perspective fit of IMG_2468. Tape one channel window to settle it

width.how: tape, 26.5 in, measured by the operator (wavemaker-f25 app/solitons.py TANK_WIDTH_MM)

depth_to_rim.how: assumed equal to the head's 42.5 in window height (one rim line round the tank in IMG_2460/2462). The photo estimate before 28 Oct was 1.00 m (IMG_2465/2464)

side_wall.corners: not measured yet: taken like the head's corner beams (2 3/8 in inner flange inside the water face)
side_wall.how: William 28 Oct: 16 windows, beams alternating 4 and 5 in starting with 4 in at the head-end corner, up to the corner where the channel meets the tall reservoir. Window width assumed from the head

frame_module.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2461/2465: post spacing from floor contact points (superseded 28 Oct by side_wall: the measured beams with the assumed 39.25 in windows)

lid_panel.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2468: spacing of the glass lid joints

head._note: The wide tank at the piston end. The channel leaves from the middle of its channel-side wall (a T, no turns). It holds the piston bank.

length_along_axis.how: tape, William 28 Oct: each long side is 8 windows of 39.25 in with 7 beams between them, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5 in (32 in), so 346 in between the corner beams. The corners are not measured yet; taking them like the back wall's corner beams (the inner 2 3/8 in flange inside the water face) gives 350.75 in. Replaces the 5-bay photo count (5.07 m)

width_across.how: tape, William 28 Oct: the back face is 125 in end to end over the corner beams; inside, the water face is 125 - 2 x 2 3/8 in (outer flanges) - 2 x 1/4 in (webs) = 119.75 in

back_wall.how: William 28 Oct: three windows between four steel beams, corners included; each beam face is 5 in (2 3/8 in each side, 1/4 in between); the windows are what is left, (125 - 4 x 5) / 3 = 35 in each, assuming equal windows

side_wall.corners: not measured yet: taken like the back wall's corner beams (5 in face, 2 3/8 in inner flange inside)
side_wall.how: William 28 Oct: 8 windows a side, each 42.5 in high and 39.25 in wide end to end; the beams between them alternate 5 and 4 in, starting and ending with 5 in at the corners

depth_to_rim.how: the head's window height, 42.5 in (William 28 Oct), taken as the inside depth from the floor to the rim. An inference: confirm with a tape from the inside floor to the top of the glass

reservoir._note: Tall blue dam-break column at the far end, behind a gate. Modelled only as a closed (reflecting) end wall for piston waves.

length_along_axis.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2466: face length / height above rim = 3.12, height from IMG_2468

width.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2468: end face about 1.0 m outside the frame; inside assumed close to the channel

height_above_channel_floor.how: IMG_2468: top 1.8 m above the channel rim; UNC Research quotes a 'three-meter water column'

tank_floor_above_lab_floor.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2465, standing camera height 1.45 m assumed

piston_bank._note: 30 pipes, 3 across the axis by 10 along it, standing in the head at the channel mouth. The bank is exactly channel-wide (3 x 224 mm = 673 mm). William's 'row n' is one group of three along the tank; in the code that is column n (display pistons 3n-2, 3n-1, 3n).

pitch_across.how: channel width / 3; the square base plates tile the bank

pitch_along.how: assumed equal to pitch_across (square base plates, IMG_2459)

near_end_x.how: bank ends at the channel mouth (operator's description)

pipe_top_height.how: William, 26 Oct: the tops are level, 56 in above the tank floor (row 10's 51 in pipe on its 5 in bottom). IMG_2459 agrees: about 0.42 m of pipe stands above the deck at rim height

row_bottoms.formula: row n bottom = 5 + 3 (10 - n) in above the tank floor; pipe length 21 + 3n in
row_bottoms.how: William, 26 Oct ('roughly'): row 1 is a 24 in pipe with its bottom 32 in (813 mm) up, row 10 a 51 in pipe with its bottom 5 in (127 mm) up

bottom_offset.how: a shift added to every row bottom, for the 'roughly' in William's numbers; `wm.py calibrate --fit gain,bottom_offset` can fit it

row_10_end.how: ASSUMED, ask William: which end of the bank the longest pipes (row 10, lowest bottoms) stand at, 'channel' or 'head'. Row n is taken to hold display pistons 3n-2..3n. The pipe bottoms then form a ramp falling toward the channel, which would steer the pushed water into it

duct_side_walls.how: IMG_2459 shows stacked steel plates closing the long sides of the bank, so water under the bank leaves through its two ends (channel and head). Set false to let it out sideways too

between_pipes_open.how: assumed: the gaps between neighbouring pipes (round pipes on a square pitch leave 25% of the footprint) are open water with a free surface, not sealed by the deck

cylinder.spec: 8 in NPS Schedule 10S welded stainless pipe, ASTM A312 TP304/304L (Felker), stencil on IMG_2458

length.note: per row: pipe_top_height - row bottom, 24 in (row 1) to 51 in (row 10)

pistons.drive: LinMot linear motors on an Allen-Bradley ControlLogix PLC (wavemaker-f25)

position_mm.how: app/params.py; -20 is the top of the travel, 370 the bottom; down pushes water out of the pipe (Model.py parking notes)

bestehorn_jerk_factor.how: makes the model reproduce the measured 3.834 s cycle of BIGGER WAVE.csv (0-350 mm, 500 mm/s, 10000 mm/s2, jerk 2000, Bestehorn), .claude/skills/wavemaker/SKILL.md

disc_face_at_0mm.how: ASSUMED, measure it: height of the disc face above the tank floor with the piston at 0 mm. Bounds: at the drive's -57 mm limit the disc must still be below the 1.422 m pipe top; at its 453 mm limit it must still be inside row 1's pipe (bottom 0.813 m). Only the length of trapped air depends on it

park_mm.how: wavemaker-f25 Model.py PARK_POSITION: after a stop the pistons rest at the bottom of travel (REST_DOWN is the default), so a run starts from 370 mm and the Prepare step lifts them to Position 1
